name: Dark Blue Green
lede: Dark blue green is a descriptive name for a deep, sea-dark teal, listed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955.

sections.title: A plain description
sections.body:
The swatch is the ISCC-NBS system's block 141 (1955), and the xkcd color survey of 2010 later used the same name [1]. Its closest named neighbor is [[bottle-green]], at a CIEDE2000 distance of 10.1 [1].

The books do not treat it as a color name, but they use the words. Ball notes that some old paintings have gone dark blue-green because yellow lake glazes over blue underpaint faded in light, as in a Lastman painting of about 1618 [2]. In 1830 Mérimée noted the same effect in Flemish paintings [2]. Salter (1869) used the phrase for green ochre, which was made from yellow ochre with prussiate of potash and resembled Prussian green [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Dark blue green is uncommon in paint. It appears in 41 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, and it is rarer than 60% of the named colors [4]. It is most often a shadow (35% of 23 paintings) or a hidden color (35%), and in the 1900s it runs at 3.5 times the museums' baseline [4]. In printed English the phrase peaks in the 1920s [5]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [4].
